key_insight: An incremental Deep Energy Method couples history-dependent plasticity with phase-field fracture using separate energy-optimised displacement and crack-field representations.
engineering_relevance: The framework predicts coupled plastic deformation and crack growth in elasto-plastic solids, supporting simulation of ductile failure.
method: Combine small-strain J2 plasticity, linear isotropic hardening and phase-field fracture with plastic-strain-dependent toughness.
Alternate energy minimisation between a ReZero displacement network and localised Gaussian radial basis functions for the phase field.
Update plastic variables by local radial return and transfer trainable parameters and optimiser states between load increments.
evidence_signal: Numerical results show close agreement with finite-element references for force–displacement responses, energy evolution, plastic deformation and crack propagation.
watch_item: Accuracy becomes more sensitive to load-increment size near abrupt fracture events.
paper_title: A deep energy method formulation for phase-field modelling of ductile fracture
